title: The TUI can browse and edit but not create or set fields

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
The curses UI can reorder, change status through three keys, and edit sections — but it
cannot add an item, and it cannot set size, tree, findings, dependencies, or (once scoring
lands) importance and urgency. You cannot actually build or triage a roadmap in the TUI;
every real edit drops back to the CLI. For a tool that ships a TUI as a front door, that
is the biggest gap in it.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: - `src/slicer/tui.py` — a create affordance and a field-edit affordance in `act`/`run`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. A create key adds an item through `ops.add` (pure-function `act` path, no terminal).
2. A field-edit path sets size/tree/findings/depends through the same `ops` the CLI uses.
3. Setting importance/urgency from the TUI works once those fields exist.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add a key that creates an item (prompting for a title, via the same editor-suspend
mechanism section editing already uses) and a key that edits a field, both routed through
`ops` so the TUI and CLI cannot drift. Keep every decision in a pure function `act` can
test without a terminal, per the module's existing discipline.

**Not in this slice:** search and navigation (next slice), reorder-at-scale (the one
after).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: A roadmap can be built and triaged without leaving the TUI.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body:
One commit: `a` create key and field entries in the detail pane (`entries`,
`panel`, `act`, `apply_edit`) in tui.py, all routed through `ops`; the five
pane tests updated to the fields-then-sections model and new create/field tests
in test_cli.py.
